text.en: The basic syllable template of Hokkaido Ainu is (C)V(C), meaning each syllable contains an obligatory vowel optionally preceded by a single consonant and optionally followed by a single consonant ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-all-hokkaido-dialects-of-ainu-the-syllable⟧. The permissible syllable shapes in Hokkaido Ainu are V, C₁V, VC₂, and C₁VC₂, where C₁ can be any consonant and C₂ is restricted to /p, t, k, s, r, m, n, y, w/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--hokkaido-syllable-shapes-refsing⟧. Ainu syllables allow only a single consonant in onset and coda positions, with no palatalized consonants other than *ch* ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--an-ainu-syllable-allows-only-a-single-consonant⟧. All consonants can occur in syllable-initial position ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-11-consonants-can-occur-in-syllable-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-consonants-may-occur-in-syllable-initial-position⟧. Closed syllables ending in a consonant occur routinely ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--closed-syllables-ending-in-a-consonant-occur-routinely⟧, and Ainu has two syllable types: open (CV) and closed (CVC) ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-syllables-are-of-two-types-open-syllables⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-template-of-ainu-is-either-c⟧. Bugaeva proposes that vowel-initial syllables (*V or *VC) are basically absent, and Itabashi similarly proposes that apparent vowel-initial syllables in Hokkaido Ainu can be analysed as having an initial glottal stop /ʔ/, yielding C₁V or C₁VC₂ shapes ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-structure-in-ainu-is-cv-c⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllables-beginning-with-a-vowel⟧. Ainu has sound sequences not found in Japanese, such as *tu*, *we*, and *ye* ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-has-sound-sequences-not-found-in-japanese⟧. There are no word-initial consonant clusters, nor clusters of a consonant and a semivowel, in Hokkaido Ainu, Sakhalin Ainu, or Kuril Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-there-are-no-word-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-structure-lacks-word-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-syllable-structure-lacks-word-initial⟧. The vast majority of Ainu roots consist of one or two syllables, and basic independent words likewise predominantly consist of one or two syllables ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-vast-majority-of-ainu-roots-consist-of⟧. Sakhalin Ainu has three syllable types: C₁V₁, C₁V₁V₂ (where V₁ = V₂), and C₁V₁C₂ (where C₂ is /s, m, n, w, y, h/) ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-syllable-types-murasaki⟧, and the permissible syllable structures are V, V₁V₂, C₁V, C₁V₁V₂, VC₂, and C₁VC₂ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-shapes-are-v-v⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-permissible-syllable-structures-are⟧. All twelve consonant phonemes can occur at the syllable onset in Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-twelve-consonant-phonemes-can-occur-at-the⟧. The minimal free forms in Sakhalin Ainu are only C₁V₁V₂ and C₁V₁C₂, while C₁V₁ exists only as bound or affixed forms ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-minimal-free-forms-in-sakhalin-ainu-are⟧. In the Sakhalin dialect, open monosyllables take long vowels such as *cii* and *kuu*, with no short vowels in open monosyllables ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-sakhalin-dialect-there-are-no-short⟧. Syllables conform to CV or CVC in Hokkaido Ainu, and to CV, CVV (long vowel), or CVC in Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--syllables-conform-to-cv-or-cvc-in-hokkaido⟧. When a high-pitched CVC* syllable in Hokkaido Ainu has C* as /p, t, k, s, m, n, w, y/, the corresponding syllable in Sakhalin Ainu is always closed, short, and high-pitched ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-a-high-pitched-cvc-syllable-in-hokkaido⟧. In words of the structure CV|CVC ending in a closed syllable, the vowel of the open syllable in Sakhalin Ainu is considered to be long and high-pitched ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-words-of-the-structure-cv-cvc-that⟧.
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語の基本的な音節構造は(C)V(C)であり、母音を必ず1つ含み、子音は先頭・末尾にそれぞれ最大1つしか来ない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-all-hokkaido-dialects-of-ainu-the-syllable⟧。北海道アイヌ語において許容される音節構造はV、C₁V、VC₂、C₁VC₂であり、C₁はすべての子音、C₂は/p, t, k, s, r, m, n, y, w/に限られる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--hokkaido-syllable-shapes-refsing⟧。アイヌ語の音節が頭音または末音として許容する子音の数は唯一つに限られ、*ch*のほかに拗音はない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--an-ainu-syllable-allows-only-a-single-consonant⟧。音節頭にはすべての子音が立ち得る⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-11-consonants-can-occur-in-syllable-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-consonants-may-occur-in-syllable-initial-position⟧。閉音節（子音で終わる音節）は普通に現れ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--closed-syllables-ending-in-a-consonant-occur-routinely⟧、アイヌ語の音節には開音節（CV）と閉音節（CVC）の2種がある⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-syllables-are-of-two-types-open-syllables⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-template-of-ainu-is-either-c⟧。BugaevaはV・VCのような母音で始まる音節は基本的に存在しないと主張し、Itabashiも同様に、北海道アイヌ語において母音で始まる音節は母音の前に声門閉鎖音/ʔ/があると見なせるので、C₁VまたはC₁VC₂の音節となると提案している⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-structure-in-ainu-is-cv-c⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllables-beginning-with-a-vowel⟧。アイヌ語には*tu*、*we*、*ye*など、日本語にはない音連続がある⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-has-sound-sequences-not-found-in-japanese⟧。北海道アイヌ語・樺太アイヌ語・千島アイヌ語のいずれにおいても、語頭には子音の連続はなく、子音と半母音の連続もない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-there-are-no-word-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-structure-lacks-word-initial⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-syllable-structure-lacks-word-initial⟧。アイヌ語の語根は大半が1音節ないし2音節からなり、自立語の基本形においても1音節ないし2音節のものが大半を占める⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-vast-majority-of-ainu-roots-consist-of⟧。樺太アイヌ語の音節タイプはC₁V₁、C₁V₁V₂（V₁=V₂）、C₁V₁C₂（C₂は/s, m, n, w, y, h/）の3つであり⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-syllable-types-murasaki⟧、許容される音節構造はV、V₁V₂、C₁V、C₁V₁V₂、VC₂、C₁VC₂である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-shapes-are-v-v⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-permissible-syllable-structures-are⟧。樺太アイヌ語では12の子音音素はすべて音節頭に立つことができる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-twelve-consonant-phonemes-can-occur-at-the⟧。樺太アイヌ語の最小の自立形式はC₁V₁V₂とC₁V₁C₂の2つだけであり、C₁V₁は付属形式としてのみ存在する⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-minimal-free-forms-in-sakhalin-ainu-are⟧。樺太方言においては開音節の単母音語はなく、すべて*cii*、*kuu*のような長母音をとる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-sakhalin-dialect-there-are-no-short⟧。音節構造は、北海道アイヌ語ではCVまたはCVC、樺太アイヌ語ではCV、CVV（長母音）、CVCのいずれかに従う⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--syllables-conform-to-cv-or-cvc-in-hokkaido⟧。北海道アイヌ語において高いピッチをもつCVC*のC*が/p, t, k, s, m, n, w, y/の場合、対応する樺太アイヌ語の音節は常に閉音節で短くピッチが高いと考えられる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-a-high-pitched-cvc-syllable-in-hokkaido⟧。閉音節を末音節にするCV|CVC構造の語では、樺太アイヌ語において開音節の母音が長くピッチアクセントは高いと考えられる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-words-of-the-structure-cv-cvc-that⟧。

text.en: Syllable boundaries in Ainu can be determined by three rules: syllables divide between consecutive vowels, syllables divide between consecutive consonants, and in a VCV sequence the boundary falls before the consonant ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--syllable-boundaries-in-ainu-can-be-determined-by⟧. Consonant clusters in Ainu occur only across syllable boundaries ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--consonant-clusters-in-ainu-occur-only-across-syllable⟧. When the first-person singular prefix *ku=* attaches to a vowel-initial verb, the syllable structures of the resulting *kuytak* and *komap* are *kuy.tak* and *ko.map* respectively, and when *k=* is attached to *omáp* the resulting sequence *ko* is pronounced as a single syllable ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-1st-person-singular-ku-attaches-to-a⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-the-1st-person-prefix-k-is-attached⟧. A syllable-final consonant often undergoes resyllabification when followed by a vowel-initial morpheme ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--a-syllable-final-consonant-often-undergoes-resyllabification-when⟧, and this process can apply even across word boundaries within the same clause, as illustrated by the phrase *cep osarkes* being pronounced continuously as *ceposarkes* ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-a-closed-syllable-is-followed-by-a-2⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-phrase-cep-osarkes-is-pronounced-continuously-as⟧. In polymorphemic forms, [y_i] and [w_u] sequences may arise due to resyllabification ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-polymorphemic-forms-y-i-and-w-u⟧. Resyllabification is blocked occasionally when a following vowel bears accent and/or across certain morphological boundaries such as reduplicant-base, with glottal stop insertion occurring instead ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--resyllabification-is-blocked-occasionally-when-a-following-vowel⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の音節の切れ目は、①母音連続はその間で切れる、②子音連続はその間で切れる、③VCV連続では子音の前で切れる、という3つの規則で判定できる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--syllable-boundaries-in-ainu-can-be-determined-by⟧。アイヌ語の子音連続は音節境界をまたいでしか生じない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--consonant-clusters-in-ainu-occur-only-across-syllable⟧。1人称単数接辞*ku=*が母音初頭動詞に接続した*kuytak*と*komap*の音節構造はそれぞれ*kuy.tak*および*ko.map*であり、*k=*が*omáp*に付く場合、*ko*は一音節として発音される⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-1st-person-singular-ku-attaches-to-a⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-the-1st-person-prefix-k-is-attached⟧。音節末子音は、母音で始まる形態素が後続するとしばしば音節再編成を受け⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--a-syllable-final-consonant-often-undergoes-resyllabification-when⟧、この過程は同一節内の単語間でも起こりうることが、*cep osarkes*が*ceposarkes*と一続きに発音される例に示されている⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-a-closed-syllable-is-followed-by-a-2⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-phrase-cep-osarkes-is-pronounced-continuously-as⟧。複合形態素形式においては、音節再編成によって[y_i]および[w_u]が生じることがある⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-polymorphemic-forms-y-i-and-w-u⟧。後続母音がアクセントを持つ場合や畳語と基幹の間などの特定の形態論的境界を挟む場合、音節再編成が阻止されることがあり、代わりに声門閉鎖音挿入が起こる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--resyllabification-is-blocked-occasionally-when-a-following-vowel⟧。

text.en: All consonants may occur in syllable-initial position, while in syllable-final position /c/, /h/, and /ʔ/ are excluded ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-consonants-may-occur-in-syllable-initial-position⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the consonants and semivowels permitted in coda position are /p, t, k, s, r, m, n, w, y/, while /c/, /h/, and /ʔ/ cannot appear there ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-and-semivowels-that⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-that-cannot-appear⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-occur⟧. Nakagawa similarly states that /c/ and /h/ cannot occur in syllable-coda position in Hokkaido Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-occur⟧, and Satō likewise excludes *c* and *h* from syllable-final position ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-consonants-c-and-h-do-not-occur⟧. Refsing lists seven coda consonants for Hokkaido Ainu — *p*, *t*, *k*, *s*, *r*, *m*, and *n* — and notes that *c* and *h* do not occur syllable-finally, and that /y/ and /t/ cannot appear before /i/ and /w/ cannot precede /u/ and /i/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-appear⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-syllable-codas-seven-consonants-must-be-distinguished⟧. Kindaichi and Chiri identify seven syllable-final consonants — *k*, *t*, *p*, *m*, *n*, *sh*, and *r* — noting that they link via liaison to a following vowel-initial syllable ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-closed-syllables-end-in-one-of-seven⟧. In Southern Hokkaido Ainu, /c/, /h/, and /ʔ/ are not allowed in coda position ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-southern-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-c-h⟧. A noun in the Shizunai dialect may end in all consonants except /*-h/ and /*-c/, which cannot appear word-finally ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--a-noun-may-end-in-all-consonants-except⟧. Hokkaido Ainu allows nine syllable-final consonants (/-p, -t, -k, -m, -n, -r, -s, -y, -w/), whereas Sakhalin Ainu allows only six (/-h, -m, -n, -s, -y, -w/) ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--while-hokkaido-ainu-allows-nine-syllable-final-consonants⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, /p, t, k, c, r, ʔ/ do not appear in syllable-final position ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-consonants-p-t-k⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-ainu-has-the-same-consonants-as-hokkaido⟧, but /h/ can ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-p-t-k-c-r⟧; Hokkaido Ainu coda consonants /-p, -t, -k, -r/ correspond in Sakhalin Ainu to /-h/ or /-rV/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--hokkaido-ainu-coda-consonants-p-t-k-r⟧. The Taraika dialect of Sakhalin Ainu is reported to allow stops and fricatives syllable-finally, as in Hokkaido Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-taraika-dialect-of-sakhalin-ainu-stops⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-p-t-k-c-r⟧. In Kuril Ainu, the consonants and semivowels permitted in syllable-final position are /p, t, k, s, r, m, n, w, y/, while /c/, /h/, and /ʔ/ do not appear there ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-the-consonants-and-semivowels-that⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-the-consonants-that-do-not⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the consonants and semivowels permitted in coda position are /s, m, n, w, y, h/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-coda-consonants⟧.
text.ja: 音節頭位置にはすべての子音が生起しうるが、音節末位置には/c/、/h/、/ʔ/を除くすべての子音が生起しうる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--all-consonants-may-occur-in-syllable-initial-position⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、音節末に現れ得る子音と半母音は/p, t, k, s, r, m, n, w, y/であり、/c/、/h/、/ʔ/は音節末に現れない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-and-semivowels-that⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-that-cannot-appear⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-occur⟧。中川も同様に北海道アイヌ語では/c/と/h/は音節末に立たないと述べ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-occur⟧、佐�ーも同様に*c*と*h*を音節末から除外している⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-consonants-c-and-h-do-not-occur⟧。Refsing は北海道アイヌ語の音節末子音として*p*、*t*、*k*、*s*、*r*、*m*、*n*の7つを挙げ、*c*と*h*は音節末に現れず、/y/と/t/は/i/の前に、/w/は/u/と/i/の前に現れることができないと述べている⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-appear⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-syllable-codas-seven-consonants-must-be-distinguished⟧。金田一・知里は音節末子音として*k*、*t*、*p*、*m*、*n*、*sh*、*r*の7つを挙げ、母音で始まる音節が後続すると連音して開音節に響くと述べている⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--ainu-closed-syllables-end-in-one-of-seven⟧。南北海道アイヌ語では/c/、/h/、/ʔ/は音節末に立つことができない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-southern-hokkaido-ainu-the-consonants-c-h⟧。静内方言の名詞は/*-h/と/*-c/（いかなる語においても語末に現れ得ない）を除くすべての子音で終わることができる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--a-noun-may-end-in-all-consonants-except⟧。北海道アイヌ語には/-p, -t, -k, -m, -n, -r, -s, -y, -w/の9つの音節末子音があるが、樺太アイヌ語には/-h, -m, -n, -s, -y, -w/の6つしかない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--while-hokkaido-ainu-allows-nine-syllable-final-consonants⟧。樺太アイヌ語では/p, t, k, c, r, ʔ/は音節末に現れないが⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-consonants-p-t-k⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-ainu-has-the-same-consonants-as-hokkaido⟧、/h/は現れる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-p-t-k-c-r⟧。北海道アイヌ語の/-p, -t, -k, -r/は樺太アイヌ語では/-h/または/-rV/となる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--hokkaido-ainu-coda-consonants-p-t-k-r⟧。樺太アイヌ語タライカ方言では北海道方言と同じく閉鎖音や摩擦音が音節末に現れると報告されている⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-taraika-dialect-of-sakhalin-ainu-stops⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-p-t-k-c-r⟧。千島アイヌ語において音節末に現れ得る子音は/p, t, k, s, r, m, n, w, y/であり、/c/、/h/、/ʔ/は現れない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-the-consonants-and-semivowels-that⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-the-consonants-that-do-not⟧。樺太アイヌ語において音節末に現れ得る子音および半母音は/s, m, n, w, y, h/である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--sakhalin-coda-consonants⟧。

text.en: In Hokkaido Ainu, Sakhalin Ainu, and Kuril Ainu alike, closed syllables are as common as open syllables ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧. The vast majority of Ainu roots consist of one or two syllables, and basic independent words likewise predominantly consist of one or two syllables ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-vast-majority-of-ainu-roots-consist-of⟧. The syllable *tu* occurs frequently in the Ainu language ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-tu-occurs-frequently-in-the-ainu⟧.
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語・樺太アイヌ語・千島アイヌ語のいずれにおいても、閉音節も開音節と同様に一般的である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-sakhalin-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-kuril-ainu-closed-syllables-are-as-common⟧。アイヌ語の語根は大半が1音節ないし2音節からなり、自立語の基本形においても1音節ないし2音節のものが大半を占める⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-vast-majority-of-ainu-roots-consist-of⟧。音節*tu*はアイヌ語において頻繁に現れる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-tu-occurs-frequently-in-the-ainu⟧。

text.en: Several phonotactic gaps are attested across Ainu dialects. The sequences *ti*, *wu*, *wi*, *yi*, *uw*, and *iy* do not occur, and where *ti* might be expected for morphological reasons it is replaced by /ci/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-ti-wu-wi-yi-uw-and⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-ti-wu-wi-yi-uw-and-2⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--where-ti-might-be-expected-for-morphological-reasons⟧. In monomorphemic forms, the sequences *yi*, *wi*, *wu*, *ti*, *uw*, and *iy* do not occur ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-monomorphemic-forms-the-sequences-yi-wi-wu⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, closed syllables ending in *-uw*, *-iy*, *-c*, or *-h* do not exist, and syllable structures such as CCVC, CVCC, or CVVC are likewise impossible ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-closed-syllables-ending-in-uw⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllable-structures-such-as-ccvc⟧. The open syllables *wi*, *wu*, and *yi* occur only at morpheme boundaries and are never found in native root morphemes, and the open syllable *ti* does not exist in Hokkaido Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-open-syllables-wi-wu-and-yi-occur⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-open-syllable-ti-does-not-exist-in⟧. Closed syllables beginning with *ti-* do not exist in Hokkaido Ainu, and closed syllables beginning with *wi-*, *wu-*, or *yi-* likely do not exist either ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--closed-syllables-beginning-with-ti-do-not-exist⟧. In Southern Hokkaido Ainu, the syllables *ti*, *wi*, *ʔuw*, and *ʔiy* are phonotactically ruled out ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-southern-hokkaido-ainu-the-syllables-ti-wi⟧. The phonotactic sequence *VC'V is not permissible word-internally across Ainu dialects ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-phonotactic-sequence-vc-v-is-not-permissible⟧. Because the syllable shape /suw/ is prohibited in Ainu, the combination /suw-pa/ from root √suw becomes /su-pa/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--because-the-syllable-shape-suw-is-prohibited-in⟧. The syllable /ruw/ is not permitted by Ainu syllable structure rules ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-ruw-is-not-permitted-by-ainu⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the syllables *wi(i)*, *wu(u)*, *yi(i)*, *-uw*, *-ow*, *-iy*, *ti(i)*, *CVVC*, and *CVVCVV* do not exist ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-wi-i-wu-u-yi-i⟧. The sequence /no/ in the modern Ainu languages occurs exclusively across morpheme boundaries as /n-o/ ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-modern-ainu-languages-the-phoneme-sequence⟧. The first-person singular nominative prefix *ku-* does not cause *i* to change to *y* when *i* is followed by two consonants, because Ainu does not permit three-consonant clusters, and the same holds when *e-* 'you (sg.)' attaches before *i* followed by two consonants ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-first-person-singular-nominative-prefix-ku-does⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-e-you-sg-attaches-before-i-followed⟧. Satō proposes that *kamyasi* 'monster' also appears as *kamuyasi* or *kamiyasi* because the cluster *my* is uncommon in Ainu, leading to epenthesis of *u* or *i* and phonetic variation ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-word-kamyasi-monster-also-appears-as-kamuyasi⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語諸方言にはいくつかの音素配列上の空白が認められる。音節*ti*、*wu*、*wi*、*yi*、*uw*、*iy*は生起せず、形態論的に*ti*が期待される箇所では/ci/に置き換えられる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-ti-wu-wi-yi-uw-and⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-ti-wu-wi-yi-uw-and-2⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--where-ti-might-be-expected-for-morphological-reasons⟧。単一形態素形式においては、*yi*、*wi*、*wu*、*ti*、*uw*、*iy*の連続は生じない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-monomorphemic-forms-the-sequences-yi-wi-wu⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、*-uw*、*-iy*、*-c*、*-h*で終わる閉音節は存在せず、CCVC、CVCC、CVVCのような音節構造もありえない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-closed-syllables-ending-in-uw⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllable-structures-such-as-ccvc⟧。開音節*wi*、*wu*、*yi*は形態素のつなぎ目にのみ生じ、これらを語根とする単語は存在せず、開音節*ti*も北海道アイヌ語には存在しない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-open-syllables-wi-wu-and-yi-occur⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-open-syllable-ti-does-not-exist-in⟧。北海道アイヌ語において*ti-*の後に子音が来る閉音節は存在せず、*wi-*、*wu-*、*yi-*の後に子音が来る閉音節もおそらく存在しない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--closed-syllables-beginning-with-ti-do-not-exist⟧。南北海道アイヌ語では、*ti*、*wi*、*ʔuw*、*ʔiy*の各音節は音素配列上排除されている⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-southern-hokkaido-ainu-the-syllables-ti-wi⟧。*VC'Vという連続は、アイヌ語諸方言を通じて語内部で生起が許容されない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-phonotactic-sequence-vc-v-is-not-permissible⟧。アイヌ語では音節構造/suw/が許容されないため、語根√suwからの/suw-pa/は/su-pa/となる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--because-the-syllable-shape-suw-is-prohibited-in⟧。/ruw/という音節はアイヌ語の音節構造のルールでは認められない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllable-ruw-is-not-permitted-by-ainu⟧。樺太アイヌ語には、*wi(i)*、*wu(u)*、*yi(i)*、*-uw*、*-ow*、*-iy*、*ti(i)*、*CVVC*、*CVVCVV*の音節は存在しない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-syllables-wi-i-wu-u-yi-i⟧。現代アイヌ諸方言において音素連鎖/no/は形態素境界でのみ生じ、常に/n-o/である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-the-modern-ainu-languages-the-phoneme-sequence⟧。アイヌ語には三子音連続がないため、1人称単数主格接辞*ku-*は母音*i*の直後に子音が二つある場合は*i*を*y*に変化させず、*e-*「お前が」が*i*の前に付く場合も同様である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-first-person-singular-nominative-prefix-ku-does⟧⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-e-you-sg-attaches-before-i-followed⟧。佐藤は、*kamyasi*「化け物」が*kamuyasi*や*kamiyasi*のような形でも現れるのは、*my*という音連続がアイヌ語では一般的でないため*u*や*i*が挿入されて語形がゆれていると考えられると提案している⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-word-kamyasi-monster-also-appears-as-kamuyasi⟧。

text.en: In Hokkaido Ainu, sequences of identical vowels do not occur, meaning that there is no contrast of vowel length ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-sequences-of-identical-vowels-do⟧. There are no (C)VVC syllables in Ainu ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--there-are-no-c-vvc-syllables-in-ainu⟧, and the Hokkaido Ainu word *toop* 'far away' is accordingly not a single CVVC syllable but a disyllabic word composed of *to* (CV) and *op* (VC) ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-hokkaido-ainu-word-toop-far-away-is⟧. When an emphatic lengthening of a vowel is grammaticalized, the VV sequence is broken up by a glottal stop and becomes disyllabic (V.ʔV) ⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-an-emphatic-lengthening-of-a-vowel-is⟧.
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語において、同じ母音の連続はなく、母音の長短の区別が存在しない⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--in-hokkaido-ainu-sequences-of-identical-vowels-do⟧。アイヌ語には(C)VVC型の音節は存在せず⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--there-are-no-c-vvc-syllables-in-ainu⟧、北海道アイヌ語の*toop*「ずっと（遠く）」はCVVCという1音節ではなく、*to*（CV）と*op*（VC）を組み合わせた2音節の単語である⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--the-hokkaido-ainu-word-toop-far-away-is⟧。母音の強調的長音化が文法化される場合、VV連続は声門閉鎖音によって分断され2音節（V.ʔV）となる⟦claim:phon/syllable-template--when-an-emphatic-lengthening-of-a-vowel-is⟧。
